subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept a custom, cooperative filesystem glob walker as the permanent compatibility boundary for existing `bootstrap-extra-files` patterns in exchange for preventing bootstrap event-loop stalls?
rationale: The benchmark supports the responsiveness goal, but only runtime owners can decide whether maintaining parity with Node glob semantics—including symlink and error edge cases—is an acceptable long-term ownership and upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Accept the walker boundary
options.body: Approve the cooperative walker as the runtime-owned implementation once an exact-head rebase and focused parity validation are green.

options.title: Keep native glob and narrow scheduling
options.body: Require a smaller mitigation around existing Node glob behavior if maintainers do not want to own a custom glob-compatibility layer.

options.title: Pause for a core performance design
options.body: Defer this PR if the team wants event-loop isolation to be solved through a broader runner or worker architecture instead.

recommendation.title: Accept the walker boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the cooperative walker as the runtime-owned implementation once an exact-head rebase and focused parity validation are green.
